links.comparator_used: Matched minimal zero-shot baseline on the same patient record, model and clinical question
links.outcome: Balanced accuracy for infection identification (three locally deployed open-weight models, two centres)
links.effect: Balanced accuracy increased in all six model-by-centre comparisons; mean differences of 3.63 percentage points at Centre A and 1.48 percentage points at Centre B
links.quote: For infection identification, balanced accuracy increased in all six model-by-centre comparisons, with mean differences of 3.63 percentage points at Centre A and 1.48 percentage points at Centre B.

links.comparator_used: Same clinicians making decisions without AI advice (paired multi-reader, multi-case reader study)
links.effect: Accuracy 92.1% with fixed AI advice vs 89.1% without; difference 3.03 percentage points (95% CI 1.47 to 4.55); 93 incorrect-to-correct vs 41 correct-to-incorrect transitions
links.tradeoff: 41 correct-to-incorrect transitions, where clinicians changed a correct decision to an incorrect one after AI advice
links.quote: In the reader study, five clinicians made 1,716 matched reader–case–decision assessments; accuracy was 92.1% with fixed AI advice and 89.1% without advice (difference, 3.03 percentage points; fixed-reader case-bootstrap 95% confidence interval, 1.47 to 4.55), with 93 incorrect-to-correct and 41 correct-to-incorrect transitions.

design_hint: structured MDT-guided prompting workflow and clinician review of AI advice
